notes: Numeric lookup plus the procedural consequence, both deep in NFM A6.4. Claims: ph-slope-test-definition-01 (56.2 to 59.8 mV per pH unit at 25 C, 95 to 101 percent of the Nernst slope), ph-ideal-cal-slope-01 (59.16 mV per pH unit ideal at 25 C), ph-slope-out-of-range-action-01 (clean, check filling solution / fill hole / junction, recalibrate), ph-recondition-triggers-01 and ph-replace-after-recal-fail-01 (recondition or replace), ph-post-recondition-reject-01 (must not be used if still outside the window). Expected to favor rag: no probe datasheet in the slice mentions slope at all — the Atlas pH datasheet gives only a recalibration interval — so the slice cannot produce a window or a remedy, and a model answering unaided tends to invent a round 90-110 percent range.

turns.content: Our pH meter prints a slope percentage at the end of a calibration. What range means the electrode is still good?

must_contain: Gives 95 to 101 percent as the acceptable slope
Gives the millivolt equivalent of 56.2 to 59.8 mV per pH unit at 25 °C
Notes the theoretical Nernst slope is 59.16 mV per pH unit at 25 °C
must_not: Invents a slope window such as 90 to 110 percent
States a millivolt range inconsistent with the percentage range it gave
Cites the Atlas Scientific pH probe datasheet, which gives a recalibration interval but no slope criterion

turns.content: Ours came back at 93 percent. What do we do with it?

must_contain: States 93 percent is below the acceptable range
Says to clean the electrode and check the filling-solution level, an open fill hole, and a free-flowing junction, then recalibrate
States that a slope still outside the range after recalibration means the electrode is cleaned, reconditioned, or replaced
States the electrode must not be used if the slope is still outside 95 to 101 percent after reconditioning
must_not: Tells the operator to keep measuring with the out-of-range electrode
Invents a repair or adjustment step the manual does not give
